docs.title: Ticket Intel
docs.text:
NLP system for support ticket routing, summarization, and insight extraction.

Welcome to the documentation for Ticket Intel. This repository provides a complete, modern NLP pipeline built for customer support operations.

docs.title: 🚀 Why Ticket Intel?
docs.text:
Customer support teams deal with massive amounts of unstructured text. Ticket Intel automatically processes incoming tickets, allowing your team to respond faster and more accurately.

  • Intelligent Routing: Automatically classify tickets into predefined categories (e.g., Billing, Technical Support) using TF-IDF and Naive Bayes, enabling instantaneous triage.
  • Auto-Summarization: Extractive text summarization distills long support threads into neat, actionable summaries via sentence scoring.
  • Deep Insights: Extract named entities, keywords, and sentiment so agents understand the customer's state of mind before they even read the ticket.
  • Instant APIs: FastAPI backend providing interactive OpenAPI documentation.
  • Analytics Dashboard: A Streamlit UI for batch processing and visualizing ticket trends.

docs.title: Architecture & Design
docs.text: Ticket Intel is engineered to be modular, extensible, and scalable. This section details the internal workings of the NLP pipelines and system architecture.

docs.title: 🔀 System Pipeline
docs.text:
The core value of Ticket Intel lies in its three primary ML models, wrapped by a fast API and a robust frontend.

graph TD
    User([User / Support Agent]) --> UI[Streamlit Dashboard]
    UI --> API[FastAPI Gateway]

    subgraph NLP Engine
        API --> Router[Ticket Router]
        API --> Summarizer[Extractive Summarizer]
        API --> Insights[Insight Extractor]
    end

    Router --> |Category| Output[(Result JSON)]
    Summarizer --> |Summary| Output
    Insights --> |Entities/Sentiment| Output

    Output --> API
    API --> UI

docs.title: 1. Ticket Router
docs.text: Currently implemented using a classic pipeline: TF-IDF Vectorization combined with a Naive Bayes Classifier. Why? It's incredibly fast to train, highly interpretable, and provides an excellent baseline model. The architecture is modularized, meaning it can be effortlessly swapped out for a Transformer-based model (e.g., BERT or RoBERTa) in the future.

docs.title: 2. Extractive Summarizer
docs.text: Extracts the most critical sentences from a support ticket rather than generating text from scratch. It uses word frequency scoring to weigh sentences. Why? Extractive summarization is computationally lighter than abstractive summarization (like GPT), and operates without the risk of "hallucinations" – crucial in a customer support context where factuality is mandatory.

docs.title: 3. Insight Extractor
docs.text:
Utilizes lightweight NLP heuristics and dictionaries to perform:

  • Named Entity Recognition (NER) (simplified) to find organizations or ticket references.
  • Sentiment Analysis to gauge if a customer is frustrated or satisfied based on keyword polarity.
  • Keyword Extraction to pull out the most important topics rapidly.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide covers everything you need to know to run the Ticket Intel application locally and in production.

docs.title: 🐍 Local Python Environment
docs.text:
Start by cloning the repository and setting up your environment:

# Clone the repo (replace with your fork)
git clone https://github.com/CCallahan308/ticket-intel.git
cd ticket-intel

# Create a virtual environment
python -m venv venv

# Activate the environment
# On Windows:
venv\Scripts\activate
# On macOS/Linux:
source venv/bin/activate

# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: 💾 The Dataset
docs.text: This project is built for the Kaggle Customer Support Ticket Dataset. Download the dataset and save it as tickets.csv in the root of the project folder.

docs.title: 🏃‍♂️ Running the Services
docs.text: Ticket Intel has two main components: an API and a Dashboard. You can run them using the provided CLI tool.

docs.title: 1. The FastAPI Backend
docs.text:
Run the intelligent routing and summarization API:

python main.py api

The API will start at http://localhost:8000. ✨ Pro Tip: Head over to http://localhost:8000/docs to interact with the auto-generated Swagger UI!

docs.title: 2. The Streamlit Dashboard
docs.text:
Run the interactive visualization UI:

python main.py ui

The dashboard will open automatically in your browser at http://localhost:8501.

docs.title: 🐳 Docker Deployment
docs.text: Ticket Intel includes production-ready Dockerfiles for both the API and the UI.

docs.title: Build and Run API
docs.text:
docker build -t ticket-intel-api -f Dockerfile.api .
docker run -p 8000:8000 ticket-intel-api

docs.title: Build and Run UI
docs.text:
docker build -t ticket-intel-ui -f Dockerfile.ui .
docker run -p 8501:8501 ticket-intel-ui

docs.title: 🧪 Testing and Formatting
docs.text:
We use pytest for unit testing and pre-commit for maintaining code standard out of the box.

# Run the test suite
pytest tests/

# Install formatting hooks to ensure commits meet quality thresholds
pre-commit install
